close_reason: Integration complete: jmap-types re-exports replace hand-rolled wire types, jmap-server Dispatcher replaces manual dispatch loop with RFC 8620 ResultReference resolution, all 18 tests pass
description:
## Why

stoa-mail has hand-rolled JMAP wire types, a 9-line synchronous dispatcher with no ResultReference support, and per-method handler files that duplicate logic the new jmap-* crate family provides correctly. The current dispatcher is a correctness gap: RFC 8620 ResultReference resolution (using one method call's output as another's input) is not implemented at all.

The sibling project at ../JMAP contains a generalized, RFC-correct jmap-* crate set. Integrating it removes the duplicated types, adds proper async dispatch with ResultReference resolution, and gets all 26 RFC 8621 method names wired automatically via register_mail_handlers.

## What

Two-phase integration:

### Phase 1 — types (low risk)
Replace crates/mail/src/jmap/types.rs with imports from jmap-types. Wire types (Invocation, JmapRequest, JmapResponse, Id, State, JmapError, ResultReference, UTCDate) are identical; this is a rename/re-export change with no behaviour change.

### Phase 2 — dispatcher + MailBackend (main work)
1. Add path deps: jmap-types, jmap-server, jmap-mail-types, jmap-mail-server to crates/mail/Cargo.toml.
2. Implement MailBackend for a struct wrapping Arc<JmapStores>. The generic methods (get_objects<O>, create_object<O>, update_object<O>, destroy_object<O>, get_state<O>, get_changes<O>, query_objects<O>, query_changes<O>) dispatch on O::TYPE_NAME to the right underlying store. Mail-specific methods (import_email, find_thread_by_message_ids, parse_email, copy_email, search_snippets) map directly to existing logic in email/ and mailbox/.
3. Call register_mail_handlers(&mut dispatcher, Arc::new(backend)) at startup.
4. Replace the /jmap/api Axum route body with dispatcher.dispatch(request, caller_ctx).
5. Delete crates/mail/src/jmap/types.rs, jmap/dispatch.rs, and the now-redundant per-method handler files that are fully covered by the backend trait impl.

## What stays the same

- The Axum HTTP layer: auth middleware, all routes, /jmap/session, /jmap/download, /jmap/upload.
- JmapStores struct and AppState.
- All storage logic — it moves into the MailBackend impl methods, not out of the crate.

## Acceptance

- cargo test --workspace passes with no test changes
- /jmap/api correctly resolves ResultReferences across method calls in a batch (was previously not implemented)
- All 26 RFC 8621 method names are handled
- crates/mail/src/jmap/types.rs and jmap/dispatch.rs are deleted
- No regression in existing jmap_basic_auth, jmap_e2e, bearer_tokens tests
design: CallerCtx for the Dispatcher should be the authenticated username (String) or the singleton user ID (i64) — whichever is simpler to thread through. Arc<JmapStores> is not CallerCtx; it goes into the MailBackend impl struct as a field. Path deps use relative paths: path = '../../JMAP/crate-jmap-types' etc. — do not publish or version-pin until the JMAP workspace is stable.
title: Integrate jmap-* crates into stoa-mail
